rv.q: The ensemble portrays Fifties archetypes to perfection, and Haydon resists any temptation to subvert that most American of themes: the virtuous outsider who prevails against the misguided mob.
And in Christopher Haydon's admirably deft revival, it proves as powerfully riveting as ever.
With its skilful structure, Twelve Angry Man commands your attention.
This Twelve Angry Men is a strong revival of an old-fashioned yet thoroughly engaging play.
The play still works; but I suspect we've learned too much about the fallibility of juries not to entertain a reasonable doubt about Rose's ultimate faith in the system.
Although not guilty of any major crimes against the theatre, this proves an underpowered reboot of a classic.
Devoid of sentimentality yet loaded with compassion, its message is timeless.

cn.t: Rose's jury-room drama remains gripping and impeccably constructed, though critics note it's showing its age. The production earns praise for its revolving set and thoughtful staging, but some find it lacks the sweaty intensity of Lumet's film.
